chunks: What ʿAlī ibn Mahziyār narrated from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Abū al-Ḥasan al-Riḍā عليه السلام, who said:
Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام said regarding the qunut: If you wish, then perform qunut, and if you wish, then do not perform qunut.
Abū al-Ḥasan said: And when there is taqiyyah, then do not perform qunut, and I adopt this.
And Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb narrated from ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ibn Faḍḍāl, from Ibn Bukayr, from Abū Baṣīr, who said:
I asked Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام about the qunut, and he said: In that in which the recitation is made aloud.
He said: So I said to him: I had asked your father about that, and he said: In all five.

So he said: May Allah have mercy on my father. Indeed, the companions of my father came to him and asked him, so he informed them of the truth. Then they came to me in doubt, so I informed them in accordance with taqiyyah.

key_terms.شُكَّاكًا: being in a state of doubt

ai.seo_question: What does al-Istibsar say about qunut in prayer and the role of taqiyyah in the Imams’ teachings?
ai.summary: This hadith discusses the ruling of qunut in salat and indicates flexibility in its performance. It also shows that differing answers from the Imams عليهم السلام could be due to taqiyyah, especially in circumstances of precaution or dissimulation.
